chunks: Al-Haytham ibn ʿUrwah al-Tamimi said to Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام:

I carried my wife, then performed tawaf with her while she was ill, and I performed tawaf with her around the House in the obligatory tawaf, and at al-Safa and al-Marwah, and I counted that for myself; so will it suffice me?

key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: around the House, i.e. the Kaʿbah
key_terms.مَرِيضَةً: ill; in a state of sickness
key_terms.يُجْزِينِي: suffices me; fulfills the obligation for me

ai.seo_question: Does carrying an ill wife during obligatory tawaf and sa'y count for one's own hajj obligation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning hajj rites. It states that when a man carried his ill wife during the obligatory tawaf and the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and counted that act for himself as well, Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام affirmed that it sufficed for him.
